sources.entry: Notesnook - A fully open source and end-to-end encrypted note taking alternative to Evernote.

summary.one_liner: Notesnook is an open-source, end-to-end encrypted note-taking app positioned as an alternative to Evernote, covering web, desktop, and mobile clients in one monorepo.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Notesnook as a free and open-source note-taking app focused on privacy and ease of use. Notes are encrypted on the device using XChaCha20-Poly1305 and Argon2 to support zero-knowledge principles. The repository holds the code for the web, desktop, and mobile clients, plus a web clipper browser extension. Shared packages cover the core logic, cryptography (a libsodium wrapper), the editor and its extensions, a logger, a streamable IndexedDB file system, and the theme. The README points to the website for a full feature list and screenshots, so this summary does not list features beyond the architecture and encryption details. It also links to an importer for moving data from other apps and to a tool for verifying the encryption claims.
use_cases: Take encrypted personal notes across devices
Replace Evernote with a privacy-focused note app
Clip web pages into notes with a browser extension
Import notes from other note-taking apps
Study or contribute to an open-source encrypted notes codebase
notable: End-to-end encryption on-device with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and Argon2
Monorepo spanning web, desktop (Electron), Android/iOS (React Native), and a web clipper
Shared core and crypto packages used across all platforms
Fully open source, with the README describing it as free (as in speech)
caveats: The README does not give build or run instructions; it refers to per-project docs and the contributing guide
The codebase is described as hybrid, with older JavaScript being slowly ported to TypeScript
The README says an email address is required, and links to a page explaining why
